issues.description: TritonLoraConfig.is_registered mutation is not thread-safe and races under concurrent requests
issues.detail: The invariant 'weights uploaded exactly once per task_id' is violated: two concurrent requests both see is_registered=False, both send weights, and only one wins. Worse, the second request may have already set the flag while the first is mid-flight. Needs a lock around the read-check-send-set sequence, or per-LoRA registration done at load time. State the invariant before shipping.

issues.description: _get_lora_config returns None when annotation says TritonLoraConfig, and dereferences metadata without None-check
issues.detail: Signature claims -> TritonLoraConfig but the function returns None. More seriously, model_metadata = self.model_metadata.get(model_name) is followed by model_metadata.lora_configs without checking None, raising AttributeError on unknown model. The type signature is a lie the reader will trust. Fix the return type to Optional and guard the lookup.

issues.description: Linear O(n) scan over lora_configs on every request where O(1) dict lookup is correct data structure
issues.detail: _get_lora_config and both _validate_*_request build a list comprehension and do membership tests over lora_configs per request. The right data structure is Dict[str, TritonLoraConfig], built once at metadata load. Wrong-data-structure: algorithm is fine, but you are paying interest on every call for what is fundamentally a name lookup.

issues.description: lora_task_id assignment is non-deterministic across multi-repo iteration and not reserved against TRT-LLM's own task_id space
issues.detail: task_id starts at 1 and increments across all repos in iteration order. There is no documented invariant that this id is unique within TRT-LLM's task table, nor that it survives a frontend restart while engines retain cached LoRAs. The reader cannot tell whether collision with prior cached tasks is possible. State the invariant or derive task_id from a hash of (model, lora_name).

issues.description: np.load of LoRA weights happens synchronously on the request hot path with no size/error bounds
issues.detail: First request per LoRA does np.load of model.lora_weights.npy inline in _create_trtllm_generate_request. For multi-GB adapters this blocks the async handler, and any IO failure surfaces as an uncaught exception rather than a typed ServerError. Pre-load at startup (the natural place given is_registered tracking) or wrap with explicit error handling and measure before claiming this is acceptable.

issues.description: Stray debug prints and traceback.format_exc leak into production paths
issues.detail: print(f"backend: {backend}") inside the per-LoRA loop, plus print(traceback.format_exc()) added to four router files and the parser's except block. These are debug aids, not literate-programming-grade comments. Remove or route through the logger. The code is correct but unreadable noise accumulates.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED with one WRONG-DATA-STRUCTURE finding. The feature works in the single-request happy path, but the central invariant — "LoRA weights are uploaded to TRT-LLM exactly once per task_id" — is enforced by an unsynchronized mutable flag on a shared dataclass, which races under concurrent load. The lora lookup paths use linear scans where a dict was the correct choice from the start, and _get_lora_config has a type annotation that contradicts the implementation plus an unguarded None-deref. Debug prints and inline np.load on the request hot path round out the cleanup. Algorithm is fine; the data structure and the invariant statement need work before this is RIGOROUS.
